functions

percent <- function(num, digits = 2, ...) {      
  percentage <-formatC(num * 100, format = "f", digits = digits, ...)
  
  # appending "%" symbol at the end of
  # calculate percentage value
  paste0(percentage, "%")
}

INT <- function(x){
    qnorm((rank(x) - 0.5)/length(x))
}

Import data

Read the csv file and claim the data type

two_level_code = c("full", "light")
three_level_code = c("full", "medium", "light")
four_level_code = c("full", "mediumHigh", "mediumLow", "light")

level2_data <- read_csv("./../results/rating/2_levels.csv", col_types = cols(

  Mental_Demand = col_integer(),

  D_easiness = col_integer(), 
  F_easiness = col_integer(),

  K_easiness = col_integer(),

    levelCount = "2",

level2_data_tlx <- level2_data %>%
  dplyr::select(ID:Learnability, levelCount)

level2_data_tlx_long <- level2_data_tlx %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = Mental_Demand:Learnability, # Selects columns that start with "Test"
    names_to = "Category",     # Name for the new column holding the original column names (e.g., Test1)
    values_to = "Score"        # Name for the new column holding the values (e.g., 85, 92)
  )

level3_data_tlx <- level3_data %>%
  dplyr::select(ID:Learnability, levelCount)

level3_data_tlx_long <- level3_data_tlx %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = Mental_Demand:Learnability, # Selects columns that start with "Test"
    names_to = "Category",     # Name for the new column holding the original column names (e.g., Test1)
    values_to = "Score"        # Name for the new column holding the values (e.g., 85, 92)
  )

level4_data_tlx <- level4_data %>%
  dplyr::select(ID:Learnability, levelCount)

level4_data_tlx_long <- level4_data_tlx %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = Mental_Demand:Learnability, # Selects columns that start with "Test"
    names_to = "Category",     # Name for the new column holding the original column names (e.g., Test1)
    values_to = "Score"        # Name for the new column holding the values (e.g., 85, 92)
  )

log_tlx_ratings = bind_rows(level2_data_tlx_long, level3_data_tlx_long, level4_data_tlx_long)

count_level <- c("2", "3", "4")

Mental Demand

log_MD <- log_tlx_ratings %>%
  filter(Category == "Mental_Demand")

log_MD$ID = factor(log_MD$ID)
log_MD$levelCount = factor(log_MD$levelCount)

boxplot(Score~levelCount,data=log_MD, main="Mental Demand",
   xlab="likert scale", ylab="level counts", horizontal=TRUE, outline = FALSE)

MD_summary <- log_MD %>%
  group_by(levelCount) %>%
  summarize(
    meanScore = Score %>% mean(na.rm=TRUE),
    lowCI = ci(Score)[2]%>% pmax(0),
    highCI = ci(Score)[3]%>% pmin(7),
    sd = ci(Score)[4],
    std = Score %>% sd())

MD_summary
## # A tibble: 3 × 6
##   levelCount meanScore lowCI highCI    sd   std
##   <fct>          <dbl> <dbl>  <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>
## 1 2               2.62  2.15   3.10 0.232  1.13
## 2 3               3.75  3.23   4.27 0.25   1.22
## 3 4               4.96  4.38   5.54 0.279  1.37
# line + dot
MD_graph <- ggplot(MD_summary) +
  geom_pointrange( aes(x=reorder(levelCount, desc(levelCount)), y=meanScore, ymin=lowCI, ymax=highCI), colour="#d68910", alpha=0.9, size=0.8) +
  scale_y_continuous(lim=c(1,7)) + 
  coord_flip()

MD_graph

MD_graph + theme( # remove the vertical grid lines
          panel.background = element_blank(),
          panel.grid.major.y = element_blank() ,
          # explicitly set the horizontal lines (or they will disappear too)
          panel.grid.major.x = element_line( size=.1, color="gray" ),
          axis.title.x = element_blank(),
          axis.text.x=element_blank(),
          axis.ticks.x = element_blank(),
          axis.title.y = element_blank(),
          axis.text.y=element_blank(),
          axis.ticks.y = element_blank()
    )

ggsave("mental_demand_levels.pdf", width = 3, height = 3)

analysis

m = aov(Score ~ levelCount, data=log_MD) # make anova-type linear model
shapiro.test(residuals(m))
## 
##  Shapiro-Wilk normality test
## 
## data:  residuals(m)
## W = 0.94805, p-value = 0.004914
qqnorm(residuals(m)); qqline(residuals(m)) # Q-Q plot

# df has subjects (S), one within-Ss factor (X) w/levels (a,b,c), and continuous response (Y)
library(coin)
## Loading required package: survival
## 
## Attaching package: 'coin'
## The following objects are masked from 'package:rstatix':
## 
##     chisq_test, friedman_test, kruskal_test, sign_test, wilcox_test
log_MD$ID = factor(log_MD$ID)
friedman_test(Score ~ levelCount | ID, data=log_MD, distribution="asymptotic")
## 
##  Asymptotic Friedman Test
## 
## data:  Score by levelCount (2, 3, 4) 
##   stratified by ID
## chi-squared = 36.651, df = 2, p-value = 1.1e-08
friedman_effsize(Score ~ levelCount | ID, data=log_MD)
## # A tibble: 1 × 5
##   .y.       n effsize method    magnitude
## * <chr> <int>   <dbl> <chr>     <ord>    
## 1 Score    24   0.764 Kendall W large
# 
# library(reshape2) # for dcast
# df2 <- dcast(log_MD, ID ~ levelCount, value.var="Score") # make wide-format table
# ab = wilcox.test(df2$"2", df2$"3", paired=TRUE) # a vs. b
# ac = wilcox.test(df2$"2", df2$"4", paired=TRUE) # a vs. c
# bc = wilcox.test(df2$"3", df2$"4", paired=TRUE) # b vs. c
# p.adjust(c(ab$p.value, ac$p.value, bc$p.value), method="holm")

pairwise.wilcox.test(x = log_MD$Score,
                     g = log_MD$levelCount,
                     p.adjust.method = "holm",
                     paired = TRUE)
## 
##  Pairwise comparisons using Wilcoxon signed rank test with continuity correction 
## 
## data:  log_MD$Score and log_MD$levelCount 
## 
##   2       3      
## 3 0.00052 -      
## 4 0.00011 0.00078
## 
## P value adjustment method: holm

Main effect on levelCounts: 2 is less mental demand than 3 and 4, 3 is less mental demand than 4

friedman_test(Score ~ Level | ID, data=level3_data_level_long, distribution="asymptotic")
## 
##  Asymptotic Friedman Test
## 
## data:  Score by
##   Level (full, medium, light) 
##   stratified by ID
## chi-squared = 37.106, df = 2, p-value = 8.759e-09
friedman_effsize(Score ~ Level | ID, data=level3_data_level_long)
## # A tibble: 1 × 5
##   .y.       n effsize method    magnitude
## * <chr> <int>   <dbl> <chr>     <ord>    
## 1 Score    24   0.773 Kendall W large
pairwise.wilcox.test(x = level3_data_level_long$Score, 
                     g = level3_data_level_long$Level, 
                     p.adjust.method = "holm", 
                     paired = TRUE)
## 
##  Pairwise comparisons using Wilcoxon signed rank test with continuity correction 
## 
## data:  level3_data_level_long$Score and level3_data_level_long$Level 
## 
##        full    medium
## medium 5.1e-05 -     
## light  5.1e-05 0.8   
## 
## P value adjustment method: holm
m = aov(Score ~ Key, data=level3_data_key_long) # make anova-type linear model
shapiro.test(residuals(m))
## 
##  Shapiro-Wilk normality test
## 
## data:  residuals(m)
## W = 0.97732, p-value = 0.00329
qqnorm(residuals(m)); qqline(residuals(m)) # Q-Q plot

# df has subjects (S), one within-Ss factor (X) w/levels (a,b,c), and continuous response (Y)
library(coin)
level3_data_key_long$ID = factor(level3_data_key_long$ID)
friedman_test(Score ~ Key | ID, data=level3_data_key_long, distribution="asymptotic")
## 
##  Asymptotic Friedman Test
## 
## data:  Score by
##   Key (A, S, D, F, J, K, L, Semicolon) 
##   stratified by ID
## chi-squared = 76.594, df = 7, p-value = 6.806e-14
friedman_effsize(Score ~ Key | ID, data=level3_data_key_long)
## # A tibble: 1 × 5
##   .y.       n effsize method    magnitude
## * <chr> <int>   <dbl> <chr>     <ord>    
## 1 Score    24   0.456 Kendall W moderate
pairwise.wilcox.test(x = level3_data_key_long$Score, 
                     g = level3_data_key_long$Key, 
                     p.adjust.method = "holm", 
                     paired = TRUE)
## 
##  Pairwise comparisons using Wilcoxon signed rank test with continuity correction 
## 
## data:  level3_data_key_long$Score and level3_data_key_long$Key 
## 
##           A      S      D      F      J      K      L     
## S         1.0000 -      -      -      -      -      -     
## D         0.4031 0.1722 -      -      -      -      -     
## F         0.0023 0.0020 0.0053 -      -      -      -     
## J         0.0031 0.0022 0.0081 1.0000 -      -      -     
## K         0.1563 0.0782 1.0000 0.0246 0.0053 -      -     
## L         1.0000 1.0000 0.6690 0.0019 0.0011 0.0282 -     
## Semicolon 1.0000 1.0000 0.7605 0.0080 0.0035 0.1199 1.0000
## 
## P value adjustment method: holm

Main effect on Level: Full is easier than light and medium Main effect on Key: (FJ) is easier than (ASDKL;), K is easier than L

4 level - easiness

level4_data_level <- level4_data %>%
  dplyr::select(ID, Light_easiness:Full_easiness)

colnames(level4_data_level) <- c("ID", "light", "mediumLow", "mediumHigh","full")

level4_data_level_long <- level4_data_level %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = light:full, # Selects columns that start with "Test"
    names_to = "Level",     # Name for the new column holding the original column names (e.g., Test1)
    values_to = "Score"        # Name for the new column holding the values (e.g., 85, 92)
  )

level4_data_key <- level4_data %>%
  dplyr::select(ID, A_easiness:Semicolon_easiness)

colnames(level4_data_key) <- c("ID", "A", "S", "D", "F", "J", "K", "L", "Semicolon")

level4_data_key_long <- level4_data_key %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = A:Semicolon, # Selects columns that start with "Test"
    names_to = "Key",     # Name for the new column holding the original column names (e.g., Test1)
    values_to = "Score"        # Name for the new column holding the values (e.g., 85, 92)
  )

level4_data_level_long$ID = factor(level4_data_level_long$ID)
level4_data_level_long$Level = factor(level4_data_level_long$Level, four_level_code)

boxplot(Score~Level,data=level4_data_level_long, main="level easiness",
   xlab="likert scale", ylab="level", horizontal=TRUE, outline = FALSE)

level4_data_level_summary <- level4_data_level_long %>%
  group_by(Level) %>%
  summarize(
    meanScore = Score %>% mean(na.rm=TRUE),
    lowCI = ci(Score)[2]%>% pmax(0),
    highCI = ci(Score)[3]%>% pmin(7),
    sd = ci(Score)[4],
    std = Score %>% sd())

level4_data_level_summary
## # A tibble: 4 × 6
##   Level      meanScore lowCI highCI     sd   std
##   <fct>          <dbl> <dbl>  <dbl>  <dbl> <dbl>
## 1 full            6.92  6.80   7    0.0576 0.282
## 2 mediumHigh      2.54  2.11   2.97 0.208  1.02 
## 3 mediumLow       3.04  2.58   3.50 0.221  1.08 
## 4 light           4.79  4.11   5.47 0.330  1.61
# line + dot
level4_data_level_graph <- ggplot(level4_data_level_summary) +
  geom_pointrange( aes(x=reorder(Level, desc(Level)), y=meanScore, ymin=lowCI, ymax=highCI), colour="#2e86c1", alpha=0.9, size=0.8) +
  scale_y_reverse(lim=c(7,1)) + 
  coord_flip()

level4_data_level_graph

level4_data_level_graph + theme( # remove the vertical grid lines
          panel.background = element_blank(),
          panel.grid.major.y = element_blank() ,
          # explicitly set the horizontal lines (or they will disappear too)
          panel.grid.major.x = element_line( size=.1, color="gray" ),
          axis.title.x = element_blank(),
          axis.text.x=element_blank(),
          axis.ticks.x = element_blank(),
          axis.title.y = element_blank(),
          axis.text.y=element_blank(),
          axis.ticks.y = element_blank()
    )

ggsave("4level_easiness_level.pdf", width = 3, height = 4)
